name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 Democratic lean in a Dallas-based seat
Colin Allred's name recognition and $8.1M raised versus minimal visible GOP resources
Open seat after Crockett's Senate run, with no public general-election polls
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97%
model.rationale: The seat's deep Democratic lean and Allred's fundraising dominance outweigh the usual open-seat risk; with no polls available, fundamentals and market pricing both point to a comfortable Democratic hold, though the margin may run a few points under the incumbent-adjusted baseline.
model.watch: Fresh polling, a shift in the national environment, or unexpected campaign developments could test whether Allred matches the district's underlying margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
TX-33, a Dallas-area district drawn to be firmly Democratic, is open this cycle after Jasmine Crockett left the seat to run for Senate. Democrats turned to Colin Allred, a former congressman and 2024 Senate nominee, who enters the general election with roughly $8.1 million raised and high name recognition. Republican nominee Patrick Gillespie shows little visible fundraising or outside support.

No public general-election polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's D+18 partisan lean, the lopsided money gap, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win near 97%. An open seat adds some uncertainty, and Allred's cash on hand is modest relative to his total raised, but the structural advantage is large. The seat remains safely Democratic, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
